{{Short description|Daily freight container index}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2021}}
The '''Freightos Baltic Index''' ('''FBX''') (also sometimes known as the '''Freightos Baltic Daily Index'''<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-29|title=Different container indexes, vastly different rates. Which is right?|url=https://www.freightwaves.com/news/different-container-indexes-vastly-different-rates-which-is-right|access-date=2021-10-08|website=FreightWaves|language=en-US}}</ref> or '''Freightos Baltic Global Container Index'''<ref name="guide"/>) is a daily freight container index issued by the [[Baltic Exchange]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-balticexchange-containers/baltic-exchange-developing-container-shipping-index-in-new-market-push-idUSKBN1HW1H9 |title=Baltic Exchange developing container shipping index in new market push |work=Reuters |date=2018-04-25}}</ref> and [[Freightos]]. The index measures global container [[freight rate]]s<ref>{{Cite web|title=Freightos {{!}} Global Freight Prices Soaring due to Container Shortages - knoema.com|url=https://knoema.com//infographics/slsatcf/freightos-global-freight-prices-soaring-due-to-container-shortages|access-date=2021-10-08|website=Knoema|language=en-US}}</ref> by calculating [[spot rate]]s for 40-foot containers on 12 global tradelanes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Container|url=https://www.balticexchange.com/en/data-services/market-information0/container-services.html|access-date=2021-10-08|website=Baltic Exchange Consumer|language=en}}</ref> It is reported around the world as a proxy for shipping stocks, and is a general shipping market [[Bellwether (politics)|bellwether]]. The FBX is currently one of the most widely used [[freight rate]] indices.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-13|title=What are Freight Indexes and How Is Freightos Index Data Calculated? What Is a Freight Rate Index?|url=https://credo-trans.com/how-is-the-freight-rate-index-calculated/|access-date=2021-10-08|website=Credo Trans|language=en-US}}</ref>

==History==
The Freightos International Freight Index was first launched as a weekly freight index in early 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Freightos unveils international freight price index, competing with SCFI|website=Supply Chain Dive|date=2017-02-27|url=https://www.supplychaindive.com/news/freightos-international-freight-index-digitization-transparency/436905/|access-date=2021-10-10}}</ref> The Freightos Baltic Index has been in wide use since 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Baltic Exchange and Freightos Group Unleash Shipping Market Visibility With First Daily Container Freight Index {{!}} Hellenic Shipping News Worldwide|url=https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/baltic-exchange-and-freightos-group-unleash-shipping-market-visibility-with-first-daily-container-freight-index/|access-date=2021-10-08|website=www.hellenicshippingnews.com}}</ref> It is currently the only [[freight rate]] index that is issued daily, and is also the only [[International Organization of Securities Commissions|IOSCO]]-compliant freight index that is currently regulated by the EU (in particular, the [[European Securities and Markets Authority]]). The index is calculated from real-time anonymized data.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Freightos Index|url=https://container-news.com/freightos-baltic-index/|access-date=2021-10-08|website=Container News|language=en-US}}</ref> As of February 2020, 50 to 70 million [[price point]]s were collected by the FBX each month.<ref name="traffic"/> The FBX was converted into a daily index in February 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Announcement: FBX01 and FBX03 Benchmark Upward Movement on 28 July 2021|website=Mailchimp|date=2021-07-28|url=https://mailchi.mp/balticexchange/baltic-exchange-circular-364511?e=42bb2e0bd9|access-date=2021-10-10}}</ref>

==Calculation==
12 regional tradelane indices are first calculated. The weighted average of these 12 indices is then used to obtain the FBX Global Container Index (FBX). The formulas given below are in use as of October 2020.<ref name="guide">{{cite web|url=https://www.balticexchange.com/content/dam/balticexchange/consumer/documents/data-services/documentation/guides/Guide%20to%20FBX%20Benchmarks%20v2.0.pdf|title=Guide to Freightos Baltic Global Container Index (FBX) (Version 2)|date=2020|access-date=2021-10-07}}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Note that the FBX calculating formula is updated periodically, with the last update issued in mid-2021.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Boffey|first=David|date=2021-08-04|title=Africa the big loser as global liner patterns shift to focus on more profitable east-west tradelanes|url=https://splash247.com/africa-the-big-loser-as-global-liner-patterns-shift-to-focus-on-more-profitable-east-west-tradelanes/|access-date=2021-10-08|website=Splash247|language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Tradelane index===
The FBX tradelanes are calculated using the median port to port all-in [[freight rate]]. This median price (freight rate) is calculated for standard 40-foot containers that are not refrigerated.

The tradelane index is calculated as follows.<ref name="guide"/>

<math>\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} ({median}(L, C_i) \times V_i)}{\sum_{i=1}^{n} (V_i)}</math>

Where:
*<math>L</math> = tradelane value (rounded to the nearest integer)
*<math>C_1, C_2,\cdots, C_n</math> = carriers
*<math>V_1, V_2,\cdots, V_n</math> = carrier volumes on the tradelane
*<math>{median} (L, C_i,\cdots,C_j)</math> = the median price for carriers <math>C_i,\cdots,C_j</math> on the tradelane <math>L</math>

For reference, a list of the 12 tradelanes used in the index calculations is also provided in the section below.

===FBX Global Container Index===
The FBX Global Container Index (FBX) is a weighted average of 12 regional tradelane indices. It is calculated as follows.<ref name="guide"/>

<math>\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{12} (I_i \times V_i)}{\sum_{i=1}^{12} (V_i)}</math>

Where:
*<math>I_1, I_2,\cdots, I_{12}</math> = the 12 regional tradelanes indices
*<math>V_1, V_2,\cdots, V_{12}</math> = respectives volumes of the 12 regional tradelanes indices

The FBX prices used are rolling short-term Freight All Kind (FAK) spot tariffs and related surcharges between carriers, freight forwarders, and high-volume shippers.<ref name="traffic">{{Cite web|date=2020-02-10|title=Insights into indices|url=https://www.marinetraffic.com/blog/insights-into-indices/|access-date=2021-10-08|website=MarineTraffic Blog|language=en-US}}</ref>
